Q: Can the same object be "rvalue-used" twice consecutively? A:

As long as the tuple is not "moved-from" I don't see any reason it cannot be used again.

But in any case I think this questions does not fit the open-ended "Advice" posts, since it should have some clear answer which is not opinion-based.

Q: Creating a folder in the SSISDB catalogue A:

As mentioned database migrated from 2016 to 2022 and the assembly on the new server has version 15, instead of 16.

This version mismatch is exactly why Error 10314 is happening after your migration. Let me explain clearly.

The “version 15 assembly” is from an older SQL Server runtime. SQL Server 2022 enforces version 16 assemblies. Recompiling the assembly against .NET 4.8 / SQL Server 2022 CLR runtime is the only proper fix.

  • Rebuild the Assembly

  • Open the original project in Visual Studio.

  • Change Target Framework to .NET Framework 4.8 (SQL Server 2022 CLR runtime).

  • Recompile the DLL.

On SQL Server 2022:

DROP ASSEMBLY [YourAssembly];

CREATE ASSEMBLY [YourAssembly]

FROM 'C:\Path\To\YourRebuilt.dll'

WITH PERMISSION_SET = UNSAFE; -- or EXTERNAL_ACCESS/SAFE as required

This ensures the assembly version is now 16, compatible with SQL Server 2022.

Q: Generate formatted diff output in Java A:

java-diff-utils

The DiffUtils library for computing diffs, applying patches, generationg side-by-side view in Java

Diff Utils library is an OpenSource library for performing the comparison operations between texts: computing diffs, applying patches, generating unified diffs or parsing them, generating diff output for easy future displaying (like side-by-side view) and so on.

Main reason to build this library was the lack of easy-to-use libraries with all the usual stuff you need while working with diff files. Originally it was inspired by JRCS library and it's nice design of diff module.

Main Features

  • computing the difference between two texts.
  • capable to hand more than plain ascci. Arrays or List of any type that implements hashCode() and equals() correctly can be subject to differencing using this library
  • patch and unpatch the text with the given patch
  • parsing the unified diff format
  • producing human-readable differences

Q: Helm: get list of the keys in a map A:

Helm includes a number of extension functions, and among these is a keys function that does exactly what you ask: given a dict-type object (like .Values) it returns its keys as a list.

{{ $environments := $service.environments | default $.Values.default.environments }}
{{ $environment_names := keys $environments }}

For the overall structure of the Helm template you show, remember that it's possible to construct additional values files and pass them using helm install -f and similar options; you don't have to put every possible setting for every possible environment in the single values.yaml file. I might create a separate file per environment:

# values-preview.yaml
server: https://sds
something: adkfgdf

# values-staging.yaml
server: https://35.246.225.83

Now if you, for example, helm install -f values-staging.yaml, then .Values.server will expand to the configured location of the server, without any of the complex conditional logic you show.

Q: Unable to Obtain EK Certificate from TPM 2.0 A:

Obtaining certificates from TPM (not from manufacturer URL)

For obtaining the/a/two/some EK certificate(s) from the TPM2 (not from the TPM2 chip manufacturer server, as the answer by MemAllox suggests), the following possibilities exist with tpm2-tools, which the question implies are being used:

Prepend all commands with sudo if they do not work without it.

One or two certificates, with convenient tool

# Get one certificate from TPM2 NVRAM
tpm2_getekcertificate -o EK_cert.bin

# Get two certificates from TPM2 NVRAM
tpm2_getekcertificate -o RSA_EK_cert.bin -o ECC_EK_cert.bin

Source: https://tpm2-tools.readthedocs.io/en/stable/man/tpm2_getekcertificate.1/

NB! Still in the beginning of year 2026, the tpm2_getekcertificate version 5.6 (which apt installs for Ubuntu 24.04) is only capable of fetching maximum two certificates from two hard coded handles(addresses) in the TPM's NVRAM.

Source: https://github.com/tpm2-software/tpm2-tools/issues/3537

More than two certificates or from any handle

To get more than two certificates or from other NVRAM handles(addresses):

# List all handles meant for certificates
tpm2_getcap handles-nv-index | grep -e 0x1C0 -e 0x01C0
- 0x1C00002
- 0x1C0000A
- 0x1C00012

# Get one (third, in this case) certificate from TPM2 NVRAM
tpm2_nvread 0x1C00012 -o cert-from-handle-0x1C00012.bin

Look inside the certificate for clues for which certificate it is

# Look under the headers
#  * Signature Algorithm
#  * Issuer
#  * NIST CURVE
openssl x509 -in cert-from-handle-0x1C00012.bin -text -noout | less

All commands are tested and verified with dTPM2 chip from STMicroelectronics, in Ubuntu 24.04.

Q: L1 data eviction to L2 A:

Intrinsics like _mm_cldemote() are builtin/inline functions that compile to single asm instructions. They asked for C/C++ "intrinsic-based" answers, which is preferable to inline asm as a way to get the compiler to make the asm you want.

Q: git: See changes to a specific file by a commit A:

git diff <commit_hash>~1 <commit_hash> -- <file path>

OR if you at the commit:

git diff HEAD~1 HEAD -- <file path>
